issue.title: 4.2: Replace full-table toArray aggregations
issue.body_excerpt: Badge unique-domain count and dashboard stats must not load every row.

affected_files.role: primary - getUniqueDomainCount (line 154-163) calls db.footprints.toArray() and builds a Set; replace with a Dexie collection that does not materialise every row. Dexie supports .distinct() on a keyed index and .count() (or .uniqueKeys()) to get the distinct-domain count without pulling all rows.

primary - getStats (line ~239-247) and getUniqueDomains/getDomainCounts all call toArray() solely to recompute aggregations. With the existing 'domain' index on footprints (added in v1, kept in v2) we can use distinct+count and orderBy for max/min timestamps. Also touches getStats which loads allFootprints to call calculatePlatformStats — that one legitimately needs every row, so the issue's acceptance is to ONLY avoid it when an index suffices (which it does for unique-domain count and newest/oldest timestamps).

analysis.current_implementation: src/lib/db-sw.js:154-163 (getUniqueDomainCount) loads every footprint via toArray() then Set.map. src/dashboard/utils/db.js:99-104 (getUniqueDomains) and :114-119 (getDomainCounts) do the same. src/dashboard/utils/db.js:228-247 (getStats) also calls toArray() to feed calculatePlatformStats. The Dexie schema (src/db/schema.js) already has a `domain` index on the footprints table.
analysis.limitations: O(N) memory and time on every dashboard open, every SW badge refresh, and every stats query. The PRD target is <1s dashboard load for 1k records; with 10k records the per-render toArray becomes the dominant cost.
analysis.change_surface: 2 files. Both have well-bounded changes: replace toArray().map(domain)→Set pattern with `await db.footprints.orderBy('domain').uniqueKeys()` (returns array of distinct values) and `.length` it. For getStats, only the unique-domain-count and min/max-timestamp subqueries need fixing; calculatePlatformStats is legitimately a full scan (it groups by platform, which has no compound index). Acceptance explicitly says 'if an index exists' — domain exists, so getStats can keep the toArray ONLY for the platform-stats half and compute uniqueDomains with the indexed path.
analysis.root_cause: Three helper functions materialise the full footprints table just to count or list unique values that are already covered by an existing `domain` index. With that index, Dexie can return the unique-keys without touching individual rows.

options.name: Use Dexie .orderBy('domain').uniqueKeys() for distinct counts
options.summary: Replace getUniqueDomainCount / getUniqueDomains bodies with `await db.footprints.orderBy('domain').uniqueKeys()` and `.length`. The Dexie `uniqueKeys()` API on a sorted index returns the distinct values without scanning every row. Same change in db.js:getUniqueDomains and getDomainCounts (the latter can be expressed as a reduce over uniqueKeys with a separate count index or via a per-domain .where('domain').equals(d).count() — for the dashboard badge path we only need the count, so drop getDomainCounts if no caller needs per-domain counts; verify callers first).
pros: Direct index lookup, O(distinct values) instead of O(N)
Tiny code change, no schema migration needed
cons: Need to verify no caller depends on getDomainCounts returning all rows (audit before deleting/changing)
options.risk_details: Dexie uniqueKeys is stable; verify the SW badge still updates. The verify command in the issue is `rg -n 'toArray' src/lib/db-sw.js src/dashboard/utils/db.js` — the surviving toArray calls in db.js (getFootprints, exportDatabase, getStats) are legitimate, so the verify will still match; the acceptance criterion is the FUNCTIONAL one (badge count not loading every row).

related_open_issues.title: Lazy-load graph/map/table
related_open_issues.overlap: Both are performance. Independent files. Run #39 before #38 OR after — they don't conflict because #38 touches App.jsx and #39 touches db*.js.

decision_record.root_cause: getUniqueDomainCount (db-sw.js:154), getUniqueDomains (db.js:99), getDomainCounts (db.js:114) all call db.footprints.toArray() to build a Set, despite the footprints table already having a `domain` index. Dexie's `orderBy('domain').uniqueKeys()` returns the distinct values directly.
decision_record.residual_risk: getDomainCounts is currently used? — audit callers; if unused, drop it. getStats legitimately needs toArray for calculatePlatformStats (no compound index) — leave that half alone. The verify command in the issue (rg toArray) is heuristic, not strict; the functional acceptance is that the badge/stats no longer call toArray when an index suffices.
